evaluations.label: A
errors: Action item owner given as 'Speaker 1', a label not used in the transcript (the project manager)
strengths: Correct numbers: 75% ugly, 80% pay more, 10% of buttons, over half lose remotes, EUR 25 retail, EUR 12.50 production
Correctly says the target demographic stayed open and lists the age ranges floated (15-35, under 65, 20-55)
Accurately captures teletext exclusion, TV-only scope, corporate colours and slogan
Correctly reports the file-sharing wrap-up: working design uploaded, project manager's presentation not on the server
Clear structure with a short summary first and timestamps
weaknesses: Action items list leaves out the individual assignments, questionnaire/summary and the marketing expert's offer to email more age data
Omits the LCD screen idea and the 65% channel zapping figure
Generic participant references make it hard to tell who presented what

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'Target group 15-35 years' presented as a decision; the group never settled on a target age and leaned toward defining goals instead
'Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery' as an action is a stretch; the comment was about whether a battery is needed at all, and the cradle was only an idea
'Chip converts energy to data' is a loose paraphrase of the industrial designer's description
strengths: Key market research numbers are correct
Captures voice recognition rejected on price and the EUR 12.50 cost limit
Covers the main agreed functions: large buttons, hidden advanced functions, loss prevention, cradle idea
weaknesses: Very terse fragments; hard for an absent reader to follow
Leaves out EUR 25 retail price, slogan, questionnaire, individual assignments and coach instructions
Action items are unassigned and miss the real next steps

evaluations.label: C
errors: Next step says 'Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder', but the working design was uploaded; it was the project manager's presentation that was missing, and the marketing expert noted it could not be saved there
'age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting' - the discussion was about income or spending, not lifestyle/attitude
Next steps carry no owners even where the transcript is clear (e.g. the marketing expert to email age data)
strengths: Most complete coverage of research detail: RSI, learning difficulty, 65% zapping, LCD screen idea, 60+ not wanting voice
Clear list of agreed functions including the find-it beep, large buttons, hidden secondary functions, battery/cradle, brand look
Includes post-meeting questionnaire, 30 minutes individual work, workstreams and coach emails
Captures price point and production ceiling and the TV-only, no-teletext scope
weaknesses: Misidentifies which presentation was missing from the shared folder
Target group stated a bit more firmly ('roughly under 65') than the open-ended discussion

evaluations.label: D
errors: Says the technical-functions presenter discussed 'potential LCD screens or sliding hatches'; the LCD idea came from the marketing expert and the sliding hatch came up later in group discussion
'Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition'; management ruled out teletext only, voice recognition was the team's own call
'Unresolved Questions' list (find-my-remote within budget, rechargeable battery as storage, advanced features within cost) is invented; these were not raised as open questions
Action Items '(none)' ignores the assigned individual work, questionnaire/summary and minutes upload
strengths: Good outline of agenda, 12:13 start and 40-minute length
Correct research numbers and Real Reaction / 100 subjects detail
Covers the components, infrared choice, cost limit and corporate identity
weaknesses: Speaker numbers (Speaker 2, 3, 4, 5) instead of roles make attribution hard to use
No action items despite clear assignments
Duplicates content between summary and outline
Invented open questions could mislead a reader

rationale: A is the most accurate and correctly reflects what was decided versus left open, including the file-sharing wrap-up, though its action list is thin. C is the most complete and very useful but misstates which presentation was missing from the server and has no owners. B is accurate on numbers but falsely presents 15-35 as the decided target group and is too terse, missing assignments. D has several attribution errors, invented unresolved questions, and lists no action items despite clear assignments.
